acceptance_checks.criterion: First verify that the CO2-rich stage dissolved a measurable calcium fraction.
After sweeping, check for increased calcium-carbonate solid and include swept carbon in the balance.

expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

original.expected_result: Removing CO2 from a bicarbonate-rich calcium solution favours renewed calcium-carbonate precipitation.
original.importance_rationale: Foundational school concept or a broadly useful experimental distinction.

initial_conditions.environment_note: A sealed or regulated headspace starts with finite ambient air, not vacuum.
initial_conditions.temperature_when_not_explicit: Engine default; read the first observation.

limitations: Sealing traps a finite room-air inventory; headspace pressure includes that air and water vapour. Account separately for dissolved, headspace and vented gas.

novelty.basis: New design or substantive controlled extension relative to the supplied catalogue; not a claim of a novel discovery.
novelty.distinction: Connects the gas boundary to mineral scale, rather than sweeping a non-reactive gas alone.

original.safety_context: Simulation-only script. Not a wet-lab procedure or permission to perform the chemistry in a classroom.
original.script:
# GS-007: Degassing hard water promotes calcium-carbonate scale
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 500mL
add v1 CO2 0.003mol
add v1 CaCO3 0.0005mol
inspect v1
sweep v1 1bar
wait 60s
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
inspect
original.title: Degassing hard water promotes calcium-carbonate scale
original.title_de: Entgasen von hartem Wasser fördert Kalkbildung
